executedChecks.scope: Focused offline run. Real-process controls (a driver subprocess SIGKILLs itself, exit -9 asserted): after the start marker, after a checkpoint, after the fixture child ran, after the terminal record, and while the fixture child is still running (child group then killed). Torn-write controls kill the driver after the temp record is written and before the rename that publishes it, for the start, a checkpoint and the end record. Review follow-up: publication is atomic (fsynced temp name then rename under the lock; leftover temp files ignored by readers, counted against the entry budget, swept by the next locked write); a damaged published record still refuses. Manual mutation checks (each failed tests before restoring): reconcile writing completed, admission-consumed check removed, manifest-drift check removed, unreconciled-attempt check removed, admission-window check removed, permissionRenewed true, temp sweep removed, temp-file ignore removed. A transient ENOENT on concurrent .lock creation (APFS) was fixed with a bounded retry.

outcome: A start marker is durably written before dispatch and consumes its reservation; interruption at any boundary leaves an open attempt that reconciles only to interrupted/unknown (never completed, even when the fixture child finished); a terminal record copies the observed state; reservations cannot be reused or renewed and a next attempt needs reconciliation plus a fresh reservation; manifest or fixture drift, torn/foreign/tampered/oversized records, unsafe roots and held locks refuse with fixed reason codes; zero duplicate fixture effects were observed across kills.
limits: Single-host, single-UID: hashes are not signatures and a same-UID actor rewriting a whole chain is excluded; durability depends on the filesystem honouring fsync (not tested against power loss); only the simulated backend was exercised, so effects are the fixture's own writes, not confined; no host, model, network, native containment, utility or independent-review claim; reservation shape is checked but its issuance trust stays with harness_admission; the journal records the observation hash, not the observation, so retention/purge of observations remains T012; no CLI codec (T015). The journal reuses underscore-private helpers of harness_admission/harness_observation (documented coupling); promoting them to public names was deferred because it would change input hashes pinned by earlier evidence files.
